note:
FEATURE / WORLDBUILDER / ROAD NETWORK INTEGRATION ISSUE: The project now has two important pieces that should be unified rather than extended independently: (1) the top-level Kentridge/Mounting Force macro world can describe settlements/regions and verified travel connectivity, and (2) Kentridge has already demonstrated physical Dirt roads with graded terrain and multi-strip grassy shoulders. The open `20260829-020634-000-KentridgeMacroWorldPhysicalRealization` issue also requires continuous inter-town roads. What is still missing is a reusable end-to-end road capability whose semantic input begins at the top-level world graph and whose physical output reaches terrain density, surface materials, vegetation, navigation/travel semantics, streaming/LOD, and final rendering. Do not solve this by adding another Kentridge-only spline, direct voxel-writing path, road mesh, or shader special case.

PRIMARY GOAL: Make roads/trails a first-class shared WorldBuilder feature. A high-level declaration such as “connect settlement/region/gate A to settlement/region/gate B with this road profile” must deterministically resolve into a terrain-aware physical route and then drive all lower-level manifestations of that route through shared systems. The same semantic road must be queryable by map/travel/NPC/navigation systems and must generate a walkable, visually coherent voxel road in the built world. The macro-world physical-realization issue should consume this road system; it must not own a competing road implementation.

FIT THE EXISTING ENGINE: Start by tracing the current production path for `TopDownWorldLayout` / `MountingForceTopDownWorldDefinition`, WorldBuilder composition, route/street generation, voxel density/surface extraction, terrain material/coating presentation, vegetation/ecology modifiers, and streaming/LOD. Reuse or generalize those abstractions where they already fit. Existing road history around commit `336cb6e63e19bc6039f3f89bb4d2056e2d0efb60` demonstrates a Dirt carriageway plus repeated grassy shoulder strips; treat that as behavioral/reference evidence, not as the desired long-term representation. Existing slope-material safety around commit `8cd28a5ea7133a4012a17112375f70384bee79ec` must remain intact. If the current architecture has moved/refactored, follow the production owners rather than restoring old file paths.

TOP-LEVEL ROAD / TRAVEL MODEL: Extend the existing authoritative macro/world topology so connections between stable semantic endpoints can carry reusable road/trail intent. Endpoints may include settlements, regions, gates/entrances, landmarks/POIs, crossings, or equivalent stable world anchors already supported by the engine. Keep logical connectivity separate from resolved physical geometry: the top level should express “these places are connected and this is the road class/profile/constraint intent,” not hand-author hundreds of spline points. A road profile should be reusable and should be able to express at least carriageway width, shoulder/transition width, surface material/type, maximum grade, cut/fill tolerance or equivalent terrain-conformance limits, edge irregularity/noise policy, vegetation falloff/suppression, and traversal/navigation metadata. Preserve deterministic seed behavior and source/provenance distinctions where the macro graph provides them.

TERRAIN-AWARE ROUTE RESOLUTION: Add/generalize a deterministic route resolver that transforms each logical connection into a physical centerline/polyline/spline compatible with the existing world-generation pipeline. The resolver must consider the same regional/geographic constraints used by settlement and macro-world generation: steep terrain, water, reserved settlement/building envelopes, passes/crossings, barriers, and other route constraints. The elevation profile should be road-like rather than a vertical projection onto every terrain micro-bump: smooth/grade the route, cut into high ground and fill small depressions within profile limits, and reject or reroute impossible geometry. A road may use a semantically declared bridge/causeway/pass/tunnel-capable corridor or other crossing solution when such reusable capability exists, but do not hide impossible slopes or deep-water crossings inside rendering hacks.

SHARED ROAD INFLUENCE FIELD: The resolved route should produce one reusable world-space influence/distance field (or the closest equivalent that fits the existing voxel architecture). That influence must be the common input for terrain grading/cut/fill, carriageway/shoulder material presentation, vegetation suppression/falloff, and other local road effects. Avoid separate approximations in each subsystem that can drift apart. The core should represent full road influence; the shoulder should smoothly fall to zero over a configurable transition width, optionally with deterministic world-space edge variation. This field must be chunk-safe, deterministic, and queryable without creating large numbers of scene objects or per-segment GameObjects.

VOXEL TERRAIN DEFORMATION: Use the road influence through the normal WorldBuilder/voxel terrain generation path to produce a genuinely walkable road surface. Grade/cut/fill terrain rather than simply painting a material over arbitrary slopes. Preserve surrounding terrain outside the influence, preserve destructibility/streaming expectations, and avoid seams where road segments, chunks, or LOD regions meet. The implementation should support long inter-region roads without requiring dense hand-authored control points.

MATERIAL / RENDERING TRANSITION: Replace the current conceptual dependence on repeated discrete shoulder strips with a generalized continuous terrain-surface coverage mechanism if the existing renderer can support it cleanly. The preferred fit is to generalize the existing single dominant terrain material plus coating/secondary-presentation concepts into a constrained model of `primary/base terrain material + optional secondary terrain material + scalar coverage [0..1]`, rather than introducing arbitrary N-way splat maps. For a Dirt road through Grass terrain, the road core should render as full Dirt, the shoulder should progressively expose more of the local Grass terrain, and untouched terrain should remain the local material. Where supported, coverage should influence the complete material response (albedo/pattern, normal/detail, roughness or equivalent), not only RGB color. World-space variation may break up the edge so it does not read as a mathematical stripe or voxel staircase. Preserve exposed-top/slope semantics: do not smear Grass down Dirt/Rock cliff faces or regress the coarse-slope material fix. If the renderer’s current coating abstraction cannot safely represent this, implement the smallest reusable terrain-coverage extension rather than a road-specific shader.

VEGETATION / ECOLOGY INTEGRATION: The same road influence must act as a local modifier to the shared vegetation/ecology system. The carriageway suppresses incompatible vegetation; vegetation should recover progressively through the shoulder rather than jumping from zero to full density at a hard material boundary. The top-level regional ecology policy remains authoritative for which species/types and baseline densities are allowed; roads only modify those policies locally. Do not duplicate the separate meadow/vegetation ownership inside the road system.

NAVIGATION / MAP / TRAVEL SEMANTICS: Preserve the semantic road graph after physical generation. NPC/pathfinding, player travel/map UI, encounter placement, town entrances, and future systems must be able to consume the logical/resolved road data rather than reverse-engineering roads from rendered voxels. Physical route resolution and rendered output must remain traceable back to the top-level connection and profile that produced them.

KENTRIDGE MIGRATION / MACRO-WORLD INTEGRATION: Migrate the existing Kentridge road/street generation onto the shared road primitive where it represents the same concept. Preserve intended layout and richer existing content, but remove any need for the old multi-strip shoulder approximation once continuous coverage is proven. `SceneIssues/open/20260829-020634-000-KentridgeMacroWorldPhysicalRealization` is an integration consumer: its settlement-to-settlement hard-route graph should instantiate this shared road system to generate its continuous roads/trails. Do not duplicate route solvers or maintain a second road graph solely for Kentridge.

PERFORMANCE / STREAMING: This must be suitable for world-scale roads. Avoid replacing the old five-bands-per-side technique with an even larger primitive or draw-call explosion. Measure route-solving cost, world-build time, voxel/brick generation, resident memory, GameObject/primitive counts, CPU/GPU rendering cost, and far-field/LOD impact. Long roads must stream deterministically with the existing terrain and must not force the entire road network into the highest-detail resident set. Prefer deriving road influence analytically or from compact route data over baking huge dense masks unless the existing engine already has a more appropriate compact representation.

BEHAVIORAL REGRESSIONS: Add focused tests proving the end-to-end contract, not just helper math. At minimum cover: (1) a top-level semantic connection produces one traceable semantic road and deterministic resolved route; (2) fixed seed/input produces stable route geometry; (3) road grading respects maximum grade and cut/fill constraints on non-flat terrain; (4) an impossible blocked connection is rejected/rerouted or requires an explicit crossing/pass solution rather than producing an invalid road; (5) the same influence drives terrain and surface/shoulder output; (6) shoulder coverage transitions continuously/monotonically from road core to local terrain and does not require a stack of discrete bands; (7) vegetation is suppressed in the core and recovers through the transition; (8) route/chunk/LOD seams do not create disconnected geometry or material discontinuities; (9) the semantic/resolved road remains available to navigation/map/travel consumers; and (10) existing Kentridge road connectivity remains valid after migration.

VISUAL INSPECTION IS REQUIRED: This issue may not close on unit tests or debug visualization alone. Validate the exact built application and capture durable evidence from the actual WorldBuilder-generated Kentridge/macro world. Required evidence includes: (a) an elevated/survey view of at least one road generated from a top-level settlement/region connection and visibly reaching its intended endpoints; (b) player-height traversal on the road with normal collision/streaming active; (c) close views of both shoulders on uneven and sloped terrain showing a natural Grass↔Dirt transition without a voxel staircase, hard binary line, or visible repeated shoulder bands; (d) medium/far views showing no road/chunk/LOD seams; (e) vegetation absent/sparse in the carriageway and smoothly recovering outside it; and (f) route/influence/debug instrumentation proving the visible road corresponds to the same semantic connection, when such instrumentation is available. Include runtime evidence for any competing hypothesis encountered during implementation.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) roads/trails are first-class reusable WorldBuilder data flowing from authoritative top-level connectivity to resolved physical route to terrain/rendering/ecology/navigation outputs; (2) high-level code can connect stable region/town/gate/POI endpoints without manually authoring dense spline geometry or scene-local voxel edits; (3) resolution is deterministic and terrain/geography aware, with controlled grade/cut/fill and explicit handling of invalid barriers/crossings; (4) one shared road influence drives voxel terrain deformation, road/shoulder presentation, and vegetation modification; (5) the road core and shoulder are visually continuous with surrounding terrain and no longer depend on repeated discrete grassy shoulder strips as the final presentation mechanism; (6) the rendering design reuses/generalizes existing terrain/coating/surface machinery where appropriate, preserves exposed-top/slope material correctness, and does not introduce a road-only rendering island; (7) road semantics remain consumable by navigation/map/travel/NPC systems; (8) existing Kentridge road generation is migrated to the shared capability and the open macro-world physical-realization issue can consume it for inter-town connections; (9) focused regressions cover the full semantic-to-physical pipeline, determinism, grading, blocked routes, shoulder coverage, vegetation, seams, consumer access, and Kentridge migration; (10) exact built-application visual evidence proves endpoint connection, walkability, natural shoulders, vegetation recovery, and chunk/LOD stability; and (11) blast radius and world-build/CPU/GPU/memory/voxel/streaming cost are measured before closure without weakening existing budgets.

NON-GOALS: A full modern-road stack with lane markings/traffic/curbs; arbitrary N-way terrain material splatting; replacing the whole pathfinding system; final per-region road art; hand-authoring every long road as a dense spline; hiding bad terrain geometry under a non-destructible mesh; or a Kentridge-only road renderer. The goal is the reusable road/trail spine from world topology to the voxel-rendered surface.
